example: Use case: a QR code for a short piece of text. Step 1: choose the Text template and type the text, for example 'Hello, SuvoCalc!' Step 2: tap Generate — the tool draws the QR code for exactly that text. Step 3: scan it with any phone camera to see the same text appear. Final result: a QR code that, when scanned, shows 'Hello, SuvoCalc!'. The same steps work for a website address, a UPI ID, or contact details — the code stores exactly what you typed.

faqs.a: A QR code stores the text you type, such as a link, a UPI ID, or a message. Anyone who scans it sees that text or is offered the link. Check what you typed before sharing the code.
faqs.q: What does a QR code store?

faqs.a: Yes. Choose the URL template, type the website address, and generate the code. People who scan it can open the site.
faqs.q: Can I make a QR code for my website?

faqs.a: The tool creates the code in your browser and does not send your text anywhere. But once you share the image, anyone with it can read what it contains.

formula: Method: the tool encodes the text you enter — a URL, plain text, a UPI ID, or contact details — into a square QR pattern using the standard QR encoding rules. Scanning the pattern with a camera reads back exactly the text that was encoded.
howTo: Pick a template: URL, text, UPI ID, or contact.
Type the exact text or address you want the code to hold.
Tap Generate to create the QR code.
Check the preview looks complete and uncut.
Share or download the code, and test it once by scanning it yourself before printing it.
intro: The QR Code Generator turns any URL, text, UPI ID, or contact into a QR code that a phone camera can scan.
mistakes: Typing the web address wrong, so the QR code opens a broken or wrong page.
Printing the code too small for a camera to read reliably.
Sharing a QR code that holds private information without thinking about who can scan it.
Using a low-contrast printout that phones struggle to read.
tips: Always scan your own code once before sharing or printing it.
Print QR codes at least 2 cm across so phone cameras can read them easily.
For payment codes, double-check the UPI ID character by character.
Keep a high-contrast black-on-white code for the most reliable scanning.
uses: It is used to make scannable codes for website links, payment IDs, contact cards, Wi-Fi details, and short messages, so people can open them with one scan instead of typing.
